headline: High: aci can exfiltrate CRM/email data via broad network egress while awesome-prompts provides no compensating controls or runtime isolation.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: aci can ingest content through direct function calls or MCP, so prompt-like content could be passed into it if the operator bridges outputs manually. awesome-prompts is not runnable and has no I/O surfaces, so it cannot actively inject by itself. The pathway exists only through unusual operator wiring, making blast radius small.
conditions: IF the operator copies awesome-prompts content into aci prompts or MCP inputs, injection is possible.
IF aci is configured to treat imported text as instructions, the risk materializes.
mitigations: Keep awesome-prompts content out of aci system/developer prompts.
Use a fixed template that strips instructions from imported text.
Review any MCP payloads before passing them to aci.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to imported content.

B_data_leakage.rationale: aci touches CRM, email, calendar, and support data and has broad network egress, so it can transmit sensitive content outward by default. awesome-prompts touches no data and has no runtime I/O, so it does not add leakage on its own. The pair still creates a default leakage path through aci's outbound connectivity.
conditions: IF aci sends prompts, logs, or tool outputs containing CRM or email data to external services, leakage occurs.
IF the operator routes shared workspace content into aci, that content can leave the environment.
mitigations: Disable unnecessary outbound integrations in aci.
Redact CRM/email fields before tool calls.
Restrict aci to least-privilege data sources.
Audit outbound requests for sensitive payloads.
requires-engineering: add DLP controls on aci egress.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: aci supports multiple instances and can write through APIs, but awesome-prompts is not runnable and exposes no write surfaces. There is no documented shared mutable resource or overlapping write scope between the pair, so direct capability conflict is limited. Uncertainty is low because B lacks runtime authority.
conditions: IF both agents are wired to the same external CRM or sheet, write contention can occur.
IF aci instances are launched concurrently against one mutable backend without locking, conflicts can appear.
mitigations: Assign separate workspaces or API credentials.
Serialize writes to shared backends.
Use optimistic-locking or version checks where available.
Monitor for duplicate or conflicting updates.

D_cascading_error.rationale: awesome-prompts is a prompt repository, not a runnable agent, so it does not automatically consume aci output or take actions. aci can produce CRM/email content, but there is no default downstream executor in B. The main cascade requires manual reuse of aci output, so the blast radius is limited.
conditions: IF aci output is manually pasted into a prompt derived from awesome-prompts, errors can propagate.
IF an operator treats aci-generated facts as authoritative without review, downstream mistakes can spread.
mitigations: Require human review before reusing aci output.
Separate fact extraction from action execution.
Use a checklist for any copied content.
Mark generated text as untrusted in workflows.

E_compliance.rationale: aci handles email, CRM, calendar, and support data and can egress broadly, which raises residency and retention concerns. awesome-prompts has no data handling or runtime I/O, so it is not the compliance driver. The pair's compliance risk is driven by aci's handling of regulated or personal data without documented controls.
conditions: IF aci processes EU personal data or customer support records, residency and retention obligations may apply.
IF aci forwards those records to third-party services, compliance obligations can be breached.
mitigations: Classify data before sending it to aci.
Block regulated data classes from outbound tools.
Set retention limits on logs and transcripts.
Confirm vendor DPAs for each connected service.
requires-engineering: implement residency-aware routing.
